clue.text: Restrained hit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: put in handcuffs
second meaning: struck with an open hand

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like a description of a punch held back, but each is a separate sense of the one past-tense verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to handcuff a prisoner and to give someone a light blow, so either past form fits.

clue.text: First class graceful clematis, perhaps

indicators.note: First asks for only the opening letter of the word that follows it

explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a plant that scales walls and trellises, one example of a climbing plant; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Improvised release with panache

explanation.surface: A musician lets loose an unplanned performance with flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Freestyle rap or dance is made up on the spot rather than rehearsed, so the adjective matches an unrehearsed performance.

clue.text: Scores of drivers at convocation

definitions.note: a convocation is the collective noun for these birds, so the phrase describes them gathered
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the birds whose group name is a convocation

explanation.surface: Plenty of motorists turn up at a university degree ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' looks like 'many', and 'drivers' like motorists; both belong to golf. A convocation is also a university assembly, which hides the collective noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf two under par on a hole is named after a large bird of prey, and a flock of those raptors is called a convocation.

clue.text: Spoil my first child playing games

clue.text: Nailhead in stump of pine

clue.text: Running battle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Running battle' is a stock phrase for a long feud; split apart it gives a race and an ancient fight. 'Running' stands for the race as a sporting event.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-distance race takes its name from the Greek plain where Athenians defeated the Persians in battle.

clue.text: Remove head of island in hostile way

clue.text: Tower's costly loose ends

explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tall pointed tower of a church.

clue.text: Watch intellectual report on freezing time

parts.note: a sage is a wise thinker

clue.text: Inspire structure redesigned without theologian

clue.text: Struggle for partners to take break on lake

clue.text: Maybe hampers revel with the final attempt

clue.text: Avoid drop of drink involving river

clue.text: Means to start to warm tops

clue.text: Beams at fish

clue.text: Supper soon cooked without salt deliberately

clue.text: Correspond with detectives closing case that's tracking money

clue.text: Some depict characters as legendary

clue.text: Drinks for hunters

definitions.meaning: first meaning: drinks taken after another drink, such as a whisky after beer

clue.text: Bitter end due to arguing
